title: Profiling and cost-attribution for vector-query rerank pipelines
creator: Marta Chen
description:
Goal: Add lightweight, low-overhead profiling and cost-attribution for the embeddings + rerank endpoint so product teams can answer: which routes, tenants, and query shapes drive cost, latency, and quality regressions.

Context: Current per-route dashboards show high-level request counts and median latency but lack token-level cost attribution, sample-based traces for multi-stage rerank chains, and workload heatmaps. Teams are shipping model/quantization changes without visibility into micro-impact on per-tenant unit economics.

Scope:
- Surface per-route cost breakdowns (embedding compute, vector search, reranker downstream steps, network) aggregated by tenant and route.
- Add sampled end-to-end tracing for rerank pipelines that annotate time spent in embedding generation, vector index query, result encoding, and reranker scoring.
- Provide query-shape heatmaps (sequence length distribution, embedding dims used, top-k values) to correlate with latency/cost.
- Integrate SLI/SLO views (p95 latency, cost-per-req, error-rate) and alerting for regressions.

Non-goals: full per-token trace for every request (too expensive), rewriting serving runtime now (we'll add hooks and adapters).
suggested_approach:
1) Add lightweight counters emitted at each pipeline boundary: embedding_start/stop, index_query_start/stop, reranker_start/stop; include route_id and tenant_id tags.
2) Implement sampling at 0.5% for full trace payloads; sampled traces include KV cache hit/miss, sequence length, token counts, model variant.
3) Extend cost model to attribute GPU time and network egress per-stage and emit per-request cost metrics as tagged timers.
4) Build a new per-route dashboard tile (Console) combining cost breakdown, heatmap of sequence lengths, and sampled traces.
5) Add alert rules: cost-per-req increase >20% over baseline for 1h, p95 latency > SLO, and trace-derived reranker regression signature.

Trade-offs considered:
- Higher sampling rates give better fidelity but increase storage and privacy exposure; we prefer low sample rates with configurable on-demand ramp for debugging.
- Attribution uses GPU-time proxy (kernel durations) rather than exact billing; cheaper to implement and close enough for operational decisions.

Rollout plan: start with internal tenants and Canary routes for two weeks, validate metrics vs billing data, then enable for top-10 customer routes and iterate on alert thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route dashboard shows cost breakdown with embedding/index/rerank slices
Sampled traces available in tracing UI for rerank flows (0.5% baseline)
Heatmap of sequence-length distribution visible per-route
Alerting rules fire on synthetic regressions in staging
Documentation (Console help + runbook) published and linked

notes_for_release: Feature gated by org flag. Initial rollout only surfaces internal-derived cost estimates; note in release that final billing reconciliation to be done in subsequent patch. Include runbook and opt-out instructions for tenants.
postmortem_plan: If excessive cost spike or privacy concern is detected, immediately disable sampling via feature flag and capture a 24h export of metrics/traces for analysis. Schedule incident review within 72h if customer impact observed.
